passages.text: Epilobium tetragonum, commonly known as the square stalked willow herb, is a species of flowering plant in the willowherb family Onagraceae.

The erect perennial herb typically grows to a height of {{convert|0.1|to|1.3|m|ft|1}} and can have several stems. It blooms between January and November{{clarify|reason=where?|date=July 2020}} and produces pink-purple flowers.
The species has become naturalised in the Perth and Peel regions of Western Australia.

Epilobium tetragonum is characterized by its distinctive square-shaped stem, with leaves evenly spaced in a tetragonal arrangement around the stem, giving the plant a square-like appearance. The leaves are hairless and solid green and have a unique shimmer in direct sunlight.
